headline: Australia Protects 220,000 Hectares from Mining and Logging
meta_description: Pilungah Reserve on Wangkamahdla Country now has equivalent protection to a national park, safeguarding over 220,000 hectares permanently.
summary_short: Australia's Pilungah Reserve on Wangkamahdla Country has received national park-level protection, permanently shielding more than 220,000 hectares from mining, logging,…
body:
Australia's Pilungah Reserve on Wangkamahdla Country has received protection equivalent to a national park status, permanently safeguarding more than 220,000 hectares from mining, logging, and grazing.

This landmark conservation decision protects one of Australia's significant landscapes from extractive industries and agricultural pressures. The reserve now joins the country's network of fully protected lands, ensuring long-term preservation of the ecosystems and country that Wangkamahdla people have stewarded.

The permanent designation represents a major win for land conservation and indigenous stewardship, securing the future of the region's natural heritage against industrial development.
quick_facts: Equivalent to national park protection status
